_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (SecretEnv ROCKETCYBER_API_TOKEN and ROCKETCYBER_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN; Files = the config the run really uses first, an explicit --config or ROCKETCYBER_CONFIG winning, then the 0600 credential store and the legacy config; every other config, store and profiles.json any --config or --home could mean is held with cliutil.HoldFile; CredentialHeaders Authorization; BaseURL ROCKETCYBER_BASE_URL, default https://api-us.rocketcyber.com/v3; Origins the base URL only; no StdinFlags, ResponseFields or URLEnv, because the one --stdin is feedback's free text, the read-only Customer API answers no credential and no token URL is read). credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit ends them. Every sink is routed: stdout and stderr at the descriptor; the API client (client.OutboundGuard), feedback, deliver and the probe through credkit.Transport; cache, journal, teach log, learnings audit, profile, platform profile, rate-limit lock, download and export files through credkit.WriteFile, AppendFile, OpenFile and NewWriter; SQLite through internal/credsql (credkit.SQLDriver, the MCP sql value cap set as each connection opens); the MCP server through MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP; the MCP server's CLI child through RunCommand; terminal checks through credkit.Terminal; auth set-token holds the token it reads from stdin. The 0600 credential store and config.toml are credential sources: their writes are a declared exemption, outside the kit in cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, and both are in Files.

The connector's own holder, output chokepoint, secret funnel, spelling records and body, URL and TOML-string readers kept growing per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time; the kit is one shared implementation of the leak contract, checked byte for byte against tools/maintainer/credkit (vendor_credkit.py --check). It closes the open round-2 class credential-split-across-processes: every 8-character piece of a held value is withheld per unit, so each process withholds its own half with no shared state and an unusable state directory changes nothing. internal/credwire/leak_test.go TestHalvesAcrossProcessesAreWithheld runs the built binary (ROCKETCYBER_STATE_DIR=/dev/null, ROCKETCYBER_API_TOKEN=QQQQQQQQQQQQQQQQZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ, argv QQQQQQQQQQQQQQQQ then ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ, --no-learn, both stderrs in one log); seen failing on the pre-kit tree (93a24e5bc: both halves printed with the unusable state dir, the first with a usable one) and passing after.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For rocketcyber the manifest gained: ROCKETCYBER_BASE_URL. server.json gained: ROCKETCYBER_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: ROCKETCYBER_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name. The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds (a profile, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl, the learn tables) is withheld by the shared credential kit at the sink (credkit-wiring), no longer by a connector RefuseHeld. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path, holds through the kit in its held pass, and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. These are names the kit never holds, so they stay hand-fixes. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments.

asserts.contains: func JournalArgvShape(args []string, isBoolFlag, isDeclared func(name string) bool) map[string]string {

Cmd:           journalVerbChain(rootCmd, executed),
		ArgvShape:     learn.JournalArgvShape(os.Args[1:], isBoolFlag, isDeclaredFlag),
writeTeachErrLog(fmt.Sprintf("teach: missing --query (%d args, %d resources)", len(args), len(resources)))

handfixes.summary: config.toml keeps base_url without its userinfo and query: save() (auth set-token, a saved token) and the legacy-config scrub pass it through baseURLWithoutCredentials (internal/config/rocketcyber_persist.go), so a password or query value that ROCKETCYBER_BASE_URL or the file carries is not written to config.toml. A base URL that does not parse and could hide either is replaced by the built-in default; an unresolved {placeholder} host is kept as written.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 4.34.2 class credential-persisted-outside-the-store: the generated save persists base_url as configured, environment value included. config.toml is a credential source written outside the shared credential kit (a declared exemption, credkit-wiring), so the kit cannot withhold it there; this is the one part of the old persistence filter the kit does not duplicate, rewritten on the standard library (the old filter's credential-name recognizers and held-value checks are retired with the layer). TestConfigFileNeverHoldsACredential (black-box, auth set-token on the built binary) failed with the filter removed (.review/bb-diagnostic-run.log: config.toml held the userinfo password, the api_key query value and an environment token under tenant=) and passes with it; TestBaseURLWithoutCredentials is the unit check.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated save should persist base_url without its userinfo and query.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error, leaving the file open (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs when the file was a filter pipe). The export now writes through credkit.NewWriter (credkit-wiring) and the open stays unshadowed.

handfixes.summary: sync registers no dependent resources: events (GET /events, required appId) stay a live read and a default sync never walks every detection app's event history
handfixes.why: 4.34.2 derives a per-app `events` sync dependent from the required appId query param (apps -> events). Event records carry no primary key (spec Event: appId, deviceId, verdict, detectionDate, value, valueType), so every default sync stored keyless rows and fanned out over each app's whole event history; no novel reads stored events (triage reads incidents and agents; events list / events summary are live). `syncable: false` on the resource does not reach a query-param-derived dependent, so tools/apply_edits.py rewrites dependentResourceDefs to return nil after every render. Test seen failing first: seen/events-not-synced-seen-failing.log in the run dir. (rocketcyber 4.34.2 reprint, 2026-10-30)

handfixes.summary: doctorShippedBaseURL is empty: RocketCyber's shipped base URL (https://api-us.rocketcyber.com/v3) is its real US API root, so doctor probes it instead of reporting every healthy install as an unconfigured placeholder
handfixes.why: press-traps s5: the fleet doctor replay restored doctor_verdict.go with doctorShippedBaseURL = "https://api-us.rocketcyber.com/v3", so doctor printed "not configured (base_url is a placeholder)" and skipped the credential probe on every correctly configured install. tools/apply_edits.py re-applies it after every replay; a fleet re-mint of the doctor template would restore the placeholder value: keep this entry. Test seen failing first: seen/doctor-real-host-seen-failing.log in the run dir. (rocketcyber 4.34.2 reprint, 2026-10-30)

handfixes.summary: spec.yaml keys the suppression resource on ruleId (id_field) and keeps it out of the default sync (syncable: false), so `sync --resources suppression` stores one row per rule and the default sync set stays agents, apps, firewalls, incidents; the rule-id flag example is a real number
handfixes.why: 4.24 keyed suppression on its rule id; 4.34.2's ID fallback finds no `id` in SuppressionRule {ruleId, ...}. Giving it id_field alone moved suppression into the default sync (a published behavior change), so syncable: false keeps it opt-in. Spec-encoded by tools/spec_fix.py: survives every reprint from this spec. (rocketcyber 4.34.2 reprint, 2026-10-30)

handfixes.summary: The black-box suite (internal/rocketcyberblackbox) drives the built CLI and MCP binaries against an offline RocketCyber fake that echoes every held credential in every encoding, and scans every output, file and request for a held value; a quiet fake (the same records, repeating nothing a request carried) proves each sink really writes and that no RocketCyber field is withheld by its name
handfixes.why: The shared credential kit's wiring (credkit-wiring), host pinning, no credential in files and read-only MCP are proven end to end, not per function, judged by docs/credential-leak-contract.md: secrets() is the set the contract holds (the declared secret environment, the config file's credential fields and [headers] values, the credential store); outOfContract() is the credential-named response members and query values the contract does not hold for RocketCyber (no ResponseFields, CredentialFlags or MCPArguments are declared), counted and reported, never failed. The kit withholds a unit whole, so answers that echo the held token are checked for the kit's notice and the data checks read the quiet fake. Updated to the kit in the kit adoption (fixture values that shared 8-character pieces with program text, such as rocketcyber, were renamed; the old layer's notice texts became the kit's; the whitespace-response test went with the retired layer). Under a go test timeout shorter than 60m (CI's default 10m) TestMain skips the suite and says so on stderr instead of dying mid-run as a false failure; CI therefore does not run it, the factory does (go test -timeout 60m ./internal/rocketcyberblackbox/; wall time in .review/bb-suite-time.txt of the adoption worktree).

OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.

handfixes.why: The press narrative claimed an exclusivity ('the only other tool') that cannot be backed up, and CONTRIBUTING.md requires comparisons to be accurate and verifiable. A reprint regenerates these files from the narrative and would restore the claim.

handfixes.summary: export to stdout buffers the whole export and writes it once, as --output does: the credential kit withholds a streamed unit that a pause between page fetches splits, so a 4 KB writer flushing between pages lost every later record (93 of 250, exit 74) whenever a credential was held

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
